how_customers_find_and_choose: Diners find places through the map listing, photos of dishes and recent reviews
Short videos of food being made or served drive curiosity, especially for new or street-style places
Ordering happens through delivery listings, direct chat or a phone call; many regulars prefer ordering direct
Cleanliness, freshness and portion honesty are judged from reviews and photos before the first visit
Group and family orders, gifting boxes and event catering still come mostly from personal recommendation
what_works_now: A short, photographed menu that is easy to send in chat, with clear sizes
Complete map listing with hours, location pin and fresh photos of the actual food
Direct ordering in chat for regulars, with a saved reply for menu, delivery area and timing
Replying to reviews, especially complaints, politely and quickly
A small number of strong dishes made consistently well
Pre-orders for festivals, family gatherings and bulk boxes
Counting waste and the busiest hours so prep matches demand
outdated_or_weak: Heavy discounting to win delivery rankings when margins are thin
Printed menus and flyers as the main reach
Advice to 'be on every channel' without capacity to keep each one current
Long menus that slow the kitchen and confuse customers
Generic 'run a food festival' ideas with no clear way to count the result

PK: Cash on delivery and cash at the counter are still common; bank transfer and mobile wallet payments are now normal for many customers
Ramadan and the two Eids reshape demand, opening hours and staff availability every year
Summer heat, monsoon rain and power cuts affect operations and footfall
Customers often write in Urdu, Roman Urdu or a regional language, and chat is the usual first contact
Ramadan reshapes timing: evening and pre-dawn meals, iftar boxes and catering peak
Eid and wedding seasons drive bulk and sweet orders; sacrificial-meat season affects butchers around Eid al-Adha
Summer heat makes cold chain and freshness a daily issue
UAE: Customers are multilingual and expect quick replies in chat; card and tap payments are normal
Winter is the busy season; many residents travel in summer so demand can dip
Ramadan and Eid change hours and buying patterns; the licence a business holds decides what it may sell and advertise, so the owner checks that with the licensing body
Delivery and cloud kitchen competition is strong; dine-in places win on experience and consistency
Food businesses are inspected by the municipal food authority; the owner keeps to its rules and asks it about any doubt
CA: Customers expect online booking or enquiry, card and bank e-transfer payment, and clear written confirmation
Long winters and a short summer peak shape outdoor and seasonal trades
English and French (in Quebec) matter, and many communities prefer their own language; consent for marketing messages and sales tax rules vary, so the owner checks them with a professional
Allergy and dietary labelling expectations are high; the owner checks local food rules with the health authority
Third-party delivery is widely used but takes a cut; some owners steer repeat customers to direct ordering

never_assume: A delivery rider or delivery listing
A website or online ordering link
A social page with active followers
